en: Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: my father informed me: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Nafi', that Abdullah ibn Umar narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I saw myself in a dream cleaning my teeth with a siwak, and two men pulled at me, one of them older than the other. I handed the siwak to the younger of the two, but it was said to me, 'Give it to the elder.' So I gave it to the older one."

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "One night, I saw in a dream as a sleeper sees, as if we were in the house of 'Uqbah ibn Rafi', and we were brought some fresh dates from the dates of Ibn Tab. I interpreted that high standing is for us in this world, and a good outcome in the Hereafter, and that our religion has become good and pure."

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us: Sulayman—and he is Ibn Kathir—narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah, from Ibn Abbas: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say to his companions: "Whoever among you has seen a dream, let him recount it so that I may interpret it for him." He said: A man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw a canopy..." similar to their hadith.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah ibn Utbah, from Ibn Abbas or Abu Hurayrah—Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar would sometimes say "from Ibn Abbas" and sometimes say "from Abu Hurayrah"—that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "Tonight I saw a canopy..." in the sense of their hadith.

Ibn Abi Umar narrated it to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) upon his return from Uhud and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tonight in a dream I saw a canopy dripping with ghee and honey..." in the sense of the hadith of Yunus.

Hajib ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi: al-Zuhri informed me, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah, that Ibn Abbas or Abu Hurayrah used to narrate that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) — (Second chain) and Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to me—and the wording is his: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah ibn Utbah informed him that Ibn Abbas used to narrate that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tonight in a dream I saw a cloud dripping with ghee and honey, and I saw people scooping it up with their hands, some taking much and some taking little. And I saw a rope reaching from heaven to earth, and I saw you take hold of it and ascend; then another man took hold of it after you and ascended; then another man took hold of it and ascended; then another man took hold of it and it broke with him, then it was reconnected for him and he ascended." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father be ransomed for you! By Allah, you must allow me to interpret it." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Interpret it." Abu Bakr said: "As for the cloud, it is the canopy of Islam. As for what drips of ghee and honey, it is the Quran, its sweetness and its softness. As for what the people scoop up of it, it is those who take much from the Quran and those who take little. And as for the rope reaching from heaven to earth, it is the truth that you are upon; you take hold of it and Allah elevates you through it; then a man takes hold of it after you and ascends through it; then another man takes hold of it and ascends through it; then another man takes hold of it and it breaks with him, then it is reconnected for him and he ascends through it. So inform me, O Messenger of Allah, may my father be ransomed for you: was I right or was I wrong?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "You were right in some of it and wrong in some of it." He said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, you must tell me what I got wrong!" He said: "Do not swear."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us—they said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw in a dream as if my head was cut off." He said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) laughed and said: "When Satan plays with one of you in his sleep, he should not tell people about it." And in the narration of Abu Bakr: "When one of you is played with," and he did not mention Satan.

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw in a dream as if my head was struck and rolled away, and I ran fast after it." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to the Bedouin: "Do not tell people about Satan playing with you in your sleep." And he said: I later heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) delivering a sermon, saying: "None of you should tell about Satan playing with him in his sleep."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that he said to a Bedouin who came to him and said: "I dreamed that my head was cut off and I was following it." The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) rebuked him and said: "Do not inform anyone of Satan playing with you in your sleep."

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Rawh narrated to us: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever sees me in sleep has indeed seen me, for it is not possible for Satan to resemble me."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever sees me in sleep has indeed seen me, for it is not possible for Satan to appear in my form." And he said: "When one of you has a dream, let him not inform anyone of Satan playing with him in his sleep."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: the nephew of al-Zuhri narrated to us: my uncle narrated to us... and he mentioned both hadiths with their two chains of transmission likewise, like the hadith of Yunus.
And he said: Abu Salamah said: Abu Qatadah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever sees me has indeed seen the truth."

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Whoever sees me in a dream will see me in wakefulness, or it is as though he has seen me in wakefulness; Satan cannot take my form."

Abu al-Rabi' Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Ataki narrated to us: Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us: Ayyub and Hisham narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever sees me in a dream has indeed seen me, for Satan cannot assume my form."

Qutaybah and Ibn Rumh narrated it to us, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd; (Second chain) and Ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: al-Dahhak—meaning Ibn Uthman—informed us; both from Nafi', with this chain of transmission. And in the hadith of al-Layth, Nafi' said: I reckon that Ibn Umar said: "A part of seventy parts of prophecy."
Ibn al-Muthanna and Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated it to us—they said: Yahya narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, with this chain of transmission.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us; they both said: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The righteous dream is one part of seventy parts of prophecy."

Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of that.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Abu Dawud narrated to us; (Second chain) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah; (Third chain) and Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us—and the wording is his: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The dream of the believer is one part of forty-six parts of prophecy."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of the hadith of Abdullah ibn Yahya ibn Abi Kathir from his father.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us: Ali—meaning Ibn al-Mubarak—narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ahmad ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us: Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Harb—meaning Ibn Shaddad—narrated to us; both of them from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with this chain of transmission.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Yahya ibn Abi Kathir informed us: I heard my father say: Abu Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The dream of a righteous man is one part of forty-six parts of prophecy."

Isma'il ibn al-Khalil narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir informed us, from al-A'mash; (Second chain) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The dream of a Muslim that he sees or is seen for him..." and in the hadith of Ibn Mushir: "The righteous dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophecy."

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the dream of the believer is one part of forty-six parts of prophecy."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham informed us: my father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); and he incorporated into the hadith his saying: "and I dislike the iron collar..." to the end of the statement, and he did not mention: "The dream is a part of forty-six parts of prophecy."

Abu al-Rabi' narrated to me: Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us: Ayyub and Hisham narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "When time draws near..." and he cited the hadith, and did not mention the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in it.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, with this chain of transmission, and he said in the hadith: Abu Hurayrah said: "I like shackles and dislike iron collars, and shackles represent steadfastness in religion." And the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The dream of the believer is one part of forty-six parts of prophecy."

Muhammad ibn Abi Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "When time draws near, the dream of a Muslim will rarely be false. And the truest of you in dreams is the truest of you in speech. The dream of a Muslim is one part of forty-five parts of prophecy. Dreams are of three types: a righteous dream which is glad tidings from Allah, a dream causing grief which is from Satan, and a dream from what a person talks to himself about. So if any of you sees what he dislikes, let him stand and pray, and not speak of it to the people." He said: "And I like shackles and dislike iron collars, and shackles represent steadfastness in religion." So I do not know whether this is part of the hadith or whether Ibn Sirin said it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "When one of you sees a dream that he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times, seek refuge with Allah from Satan three times, and turn over from the side on which he was lying."
